executiveSummary.headline: Turn Broad Coverage Into Clearer Corporate Consideration
executiveSummary.lead: Bethesda Marriott appears in 71.4% of eligible scenarios and ranks first among four Marriott Bonvoy peers, yet consideration is still modest at 30.1%. Its strength is relative coverage, not strong absolute selection.
executiveSummary.metricsNote: These metrics describe presence in monitored AI answers—not bookings, revenue, or traveler exposure.

themes.title: Corporate Buyers Have Strong Raw Material
themes.what: Official content already presents 19,000 square feet of meeting space, a metro shuttle, Cooper’s Mill, and proximity to NIH, Walter Reed, and American University.
themes.whyItMatters: A controlled corporate fact set can make the hotel’s practical fit clearer for planners without adding unsupported distance, access, or service claims.

themes.title: Wellness Details Can Support Longer Stays
themes.what: The property page identifies a fitness offer with Peloton and TRX, alongside dining and meetings information relevant to business and group guests.
themes.whyItMatters: Keeping these stable amenities consistent across official content and current sales collateral helps planners evaluate the complete business stay experience with greater confidence.

themes.title: Technical and Competitive Signals Need Review
themes.what: Akamai returned a 403 to one automated GET while robots.txt was available and did not disallow the path; Hyatt Regency Bethesda also displaced the hotel in ADP.
themes.whyItMatters: Neither signal proves a defect or competitive cause, so targeted, documented investigation should precede platform or positioning changes.

priorities.action: Build a corporate and meetings source of truth

executiveSummary.successLooksLike: Corporate, meetings, local-access, dining, and fitness facts are approved and consistent; technical and competitive questions have documented outcomes; optional content proceeds only with sales support.
executiveSummary.closing: Executive Takeaway: Bethesda Marriott has broad relative coverage but still appears in fewer than one-third of monitored consideration answers. Protect the strong official fact base, sharpen only the corporate distinctions supported by hotel evidence, and investigate access and Hyatt displacement without assuming causation.

actions.headline: Investigate Marriott Property-Page Access for Intended Crawlers
actions.priorityWhy: The observed GET behavior differs from the available robots policy but may be environment-specific.
actions.whatWeFound: Marriott robots.txt returned 200 and did not disallow the property overview path; an automated GET redirected to default.mi and returned Akamai 403, while HEAD returned 200.
actions.whyItMatters: Platform review should determine intended behavior before any security change. This bounded observation is not proof that guests, search engines, or AI systems are universally blocked.
recommendedSteps: Open a Marriott platform ticket with timestamps and redirects.
Confirm intended crawler policy for the property path.
Retest with agreed clients and regions.
Document expected behavior or narrowly approved remediation.

actions.headline: Decide Whether to Add an Association and Corporate Module
actions.priorityWhy: The official site already carries substantial corporate content; a new module is a commercial choice, not a defect correction.
actions.whatWeFound: The property already presents meetings, shuttle, dining, fitness, and institutional proximity. A dedicated association or local-corporate module should be considered only if sales wants that audience.
actions.whyItMatters: A focused module could organize buyer-relevant facts and inquiry routing, but generic expansion would add maintenance without a clear commercial purpose.
recommendedSteps: Sales makes a segment-level go/no-go decision.
If go, define buyer, use cases, approved facts, and inquiry owner.
Draft a concise module without duplicating generic brand copy.
If no-go, document and close the action.

actions.suggestedTimeframe: Decision within 30 days; module in 60–90 days if approved
actions.timeframeNote: Timing is proposed and requires accountable-owner agreement.

changesOrInvestigation: Define the target planner and qualifying use cases.
Reuse only hotel-approved meeting, access, dining, and fitness facts.
Assign inquiry routing and content owner.
Do not build if sales records a no-go.
technicalDetails.verificationMethod: Decision memo; if approved, live-module QA against the signed brief.
dependencies: Commercial go/no-go and factual sign-off are required before content production.
technicalDetails.notes: No paid research or ADP remeasurement was performed.

methodology.scope: Combines the certified ADP baseline with a bounded review of named public pages and zero-cost technical probes. No paid research, Airtable write, ADP remeasurement, or customer publication was performed.
claimTypeGuide: VERIFIED_ISSUE — a directly observed, source-backed discrepancy.
RECOMMENDED_INVESTIGATION — evidence warrants review but does not prove a defect or cause.
REQUIRES_HOTEL_CONFIRMATION — hotel leadership must establish the source of truth before correction.
OPTIONAL_COMMERCIAL_OPPORTUNITY — proceed only if leadership wants the demand.
responsibilities: Hotel leadership confirms facts, priorities, and public changes.
Digital or brand teams implement only approved corrections and document verification.
Dealality packages measurement context and evidence without implying booking or revenue causation.
methodology.monthlyReviewRelationship: Approved actions may be tracked in a later review. Completing an action does not itself prove a change in AI presence, bookings, or revenue.
methodology.nextStep: Confirm the decision items, then authorize the highest-priority validated work.
